label: Safe R

model.rationale: This is a heavily Republican Utah seat with an incumbent who has out-raised his Democratic opponent roughly eighteen-to-one, and no polls or expert ratings suggest any competitive threat. Markets price a Republican win near certainty, consistent with the district's fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late independent spending or polling showing Larsen within single digits would warrant a re-examination, but nothing currently indicates such a shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Utah's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 17 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Mike Kennedy is running for re-election and holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised roughly $970,000 with $387,000 on hand. Democratic challenger Jonny Larsen has raised about $54,000 and reported just over $1,100 in cash, with no outside spending on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and fundraising. Prediction markets give Kennedy about a 95% chance of winning. The race is rated Safe Republican, with an expected margin near 17 points in Kennedy's favor.
